lessons.title: Snowshoes or mini-skis?
lessons.intro: This chapter shows the complete switch between snowshoe mode for walking uphill and mini-ski mode for riding down. The binding has keyhole-shaped mounting slots. The front slot is at the boot toe and the rear slot at the boot heel, in both modes.

points.text: In snowshoe mode, the side with the metal rim and metal spikes always points forward. The plastic tip must never be at the front.
This is incorrect: the plastic tip must not point forward in snowshoe mode.
In snowshoe mode, attach the front keyhole-shaped mounting slot (at the boot toe) to the middle pin on each side. The front pin remains unused, allowing the heel to move slightly.
In mini-ski mode, the binding is secured at both the front and rear.
First attach the rear mounting slot, at the boot heel.
Then attach the front mounting slot with the release button, at the boot toe.

questions.question: Which side points forward in snowshoe mode?
answers: The side with the metal rim and spikes
questions.hint: The side with the metal rim and metal spikes always points forward.

questions.question: What is secured on the middle pin in snowshoe mode?
answers: Only the front mounting slot (at the boot toe), so the heel can move slightly
Only the rear mounting slot (at the boot heel)
questions.hint: Attach only the front mounting slot to the middle pin on each side, so the heel can move slightly.

questions.question: In which order is the binding attached in mini-ski mode?
answers: Front mounting slot first, then rear
Rear mounting slot first, then the front slot with the release button
questions.hint: Attach the rear mounting slot first, then the front slot with the release button.

lessons.title: Adjustment and correct fit
lessons.intro: Set the size and check the L and R marks before putting Combo Ski on. The fabric heel strap adjusts the size and the position of the boot. The front ratchet strap goes over the toes. The rear ratchet strap goes over the top of the foot. The upper Velcro strap goes around the shin.

points.text: Always check that the left binding is on the left foot and the right binding on the right foot. The L and R markings are on the Velcro strap.
Use the heel textile strap to position the boot so the heel aligns with the marked positions S, M or L according to the size chart.
Repeat the process on the other side of the binding.
Tighten both straps securely, as if Combo Ski were a solid part of the boot.

questions.question: How do you identify left and right?
answers: By the L and R markings on the Velcro strap
questions.hint: The L and R markings are on the Velcro strap.

questions.question: What must be adjusted correctly for the boot size?
questions.hint: Adjust the heel textile strap so the heel matches the marked size.

questions.question: How should you tighten the front and rear ratchet straps before riding?
answers: Tighten both firmly, as if Combo Ski were a solid part of the boot
Tightening only the front strap is enough

lessons.title: Stance, turning and braking
lessons.intro: Start on flat ground, then move to a gentle slope. First learn a stable stance, turning and safe braking.

points.text: We recommend wearing a ski helmet.
Keep your feet together and your knees bent. Balance forwards and backwards, as on ice skates or inline skates. Do not lean back.
Turn as on normal skis, or move one foot slightly in front of the other.
To brake, turn both mini-skis sideways and slide on their edges, as on ice skates. If you cannot stop, use a controlled fall.

questions.question: Where should you start?
answers: On flat ground, then on a gentle slope
questions.hint: Start on flat ground, then move to a gentle slope.

questions.question: What is the basic stance?
questions.hint: Keep your feet together and your knees bent. Do not lean back.

questions.question: How should you brake?
answers: Turn both mini-skis sideways and slide on their edges, as on ice skates
questions.hint: Turn both mini-skis sideways and slide on their edges.

lessons.title: Surface, footwear and control
lessons.intro: Behaviour changes with the surface. Practise gradually and match the conditions to your ability.

points.text: Avoid icy or frozen snow and rocks.
Sturdy high-ankle winter boots improve support and control.
Practise balance first, then progress to skating and gentle descents.

questions.question: What surface should you avoid?
questions.hint: Avoid icy or frozen snow and rocks.

questions.question: What should you practise first?
questions.hint: Practise balance and basic stance first.

lessons.title: Back to snowshoes and uphill
lessons.intro: Change mode on level ground and make sure the heel remains free.

points.text: Clear snow or ice from the keyholes and pins, for example by blowing it out.
To release the binding, press the button and slide the mounting slot down off the pin.
Turn Combo Ski base-up and place the binding on the middle pin.
Attach the front keyhole-shaped mounting slot (at the boot toe) to the middle pin on each side.
Keep the heel free for a more natural step.
Use the heel textile strap to align the boot tip with the tip of Combo Ski.
Tighten the straps in this order: first the front strap over the toes, then the rear strap over the top of the foot, and finally the upper Velcro strap around the shin.

questions.question: What should you do if the keyholes or pins contain snow or ice?
answers: Clear them, for example by blowing it out
questions.hint: Clear the keyholes and pins first, for example by blowing out the snow.

questions.question: In what order should you tighten the straps in snowshoe mode?
answers: Rear strap first, then front strap
Front strap over the toes, rear strap over the top of the foot, then upper Velcro strap
questions.hint: Front strap over the toes, rear strap over the top of the foot, then upper Velcro strap.

questions.question: Where should the boot toe be in snowshoe mode?
answers: Aligned with the tip of Combo Ski
Far behind the Combo Ski tip
Outside the Combo Ski centre line
questions.hint: Align the boot tip with the tip of Combo Ski.

questions.question: What is secured on the middle pin in snowshoe mode?
answers: Only the front mounting slot (at the boot toe), so the heel can move slightly
Only the rear mounting slot (at the boot heel)
questions.hint: Attach only the front mounting slot to the middle pin on each side, so the heel can move slightly.

lessons.title: Dry and inspect after use
lessons.intro: Drying, inspection and correct storage protect the bases and extend product life.

points.text: Let Combo Ski dry completely after every use. Do not store them wet.
When carrying or packing Combo Ski in a backpack, position them so the metal teeth cannot damage the sliding surface.
Check screw connections regularly.
Stop using damaged parts and contact service.

questions.question: What should you do after use?
How should they be packed?
answers: So the metal teeth cannot damage the sliding surface
questions.hint: Position Combo Ski so the metal teeth cannot damage the sliding surface.

questions.question: What if a part is damaged?
answers: Stop using it and contact service at info@comboski.cz
questions.hint: Do not use a damaged product; contact service at info@comboski.cz.

subtitles.text: Hi, I’m Vojta, and today I’ll show you,
how to safely use Combo Ski
and our Sever Gear poles.
Combo Ski can be used in two modes.
Snowshoe mode or mini-ski mode.
In snowshoe mode, I attach only the middle pin
to the front keyhole-shaped mounting slot.
In snowshoe mode, the metal spikes must always be at the front,
The plastic end stays
at the back, never at the front.
As I mentioned,
I connect only one pin,
The front pin remains unused.
Now let’s switch to mini-ski mode.
I release the pin,
and release the mounting slot on the other side too.
and now I connect both pins.
First the rear mounting slot, then the front one.
The same on the other side.
Now I need to adjust the textile heel strap
so that the size fits me.
For example,
I set my Combo Ski between size S and M.
So I loosen the plastic buckle,
and adjust the strap to fit comfortably.
I do the same on the other Combo Ski.
Now I put the Combo Ski on my right foot,
The R mark is
on the upper Velcro strap.
I tighten the straps firmly,
using the buckle.
The front strap over the toes,
then the upper Velcro strap.
I do the same on the left foot.
While standing, I tighten the straps,
so that Combo Ski feels like a solid part of the boot.
I check the heel strap used to adjust the size.
The upper strap
can sit either on the boot,
or directly on the leg. Both are correct.
Now let’s show how to ride downhill on Combo Ski.
Never start,
on steep slopes or red ski runs.
It’s always better to start on flat terrain or gentle slopes.
Always make sure,
you are not tense,
stay relaxed and keep your knees bent.
I keep my knees bent,
make short turns,
For better balance, I keep one foot
slightly in front of the other.
At first, it may feel awkward,
but over time you get used to it,
gain confidence and use the hockey stop to brake.
As I mentioned,
Keep one foot slightly in front of the other for better balance.
Common mistakes.
Never ski with straight legs or try to snowplough.
It doesn’t work and you are likely to fall.
The key is to stay relaxed,
especially in your knees.
After a short practice, you can increase speed and slope angle,
and start enjoying the ride more.
As you can see,
thanks to the edges and the upper strap,
the ride is comfortable and safe.
One of the most fun movements on Combo Ski is skating.
At the same time, it’s one of the easiest ways,
to learn Combo Ski.
It helps you balance forwards and backwards:
you skate just as you would on inline skates.
you can skate downhill,
or on flat terrain,
or even,
slightly uphill.
When riding downhill, snow conditions are very important,
the best conditions are normal, soft snow.
Icy surfaces are dangerous and difficult.
Riding on ice is almost impossible for beginners.
Sturdy winter boots are ideal for Combo Ski.
There is only one rule,
They must support the ankle.
The higher and stiffer the boots are,
the better.
Now I switch Combo Ski to snowshoe mode.
I press the button,
and release the rear slot.
and do the same on the other side.
And now, as I mentioned earlier,
the most important thing is,
that the metal spikes are at the front.
So I attach only the middle pin
and press it in.
If there is snow inside,
I simply blow it out,
and do the same on the other side.
This is how snowshoe mode is set.
As you can see,
I am now inserting my right foot.
I slide my foot fully back and check
that the textile heel strap is seated securely.
I tighten the front strap over the toes,
then the rear strap over the top of the foot,
and finally the upper Velcro strap.
As you can see,
the toe of the boot is aligned with the tip of Combo Ski.
This means Combo Ski is correctly fitted.
I can comfortably walk uphill.
On very steep terrain,
don’t hesitate to dig Combo Ski into the snow.
